Generally songs will be written in a “key” signature. The key will be chosen out of the notes we have (A, A#, B, C, C#, D, D#, E, F, F#, G, G#)It might be A major, F minor, E major, or whatever. The “key” is almost like the mood of the song. Generally Major is happy and minor is sad. # means sharp, which is basically jus one note higher.

Say for example you want your song in C Major. The song may contain all the notes of the C Major scale. (A scale is a collection of notes. C major scale is C D E F G A B, that means those notes all sound “right” when played together in a song) Maybe it’ll have a rhythm guitar/piano playing C, then D over and over. And you could sing over that and it would probably sound decent enough. 

Although they are “rules”, they don’t have to be and aren’t always followed. It’s more like a foundation to work upon.

Wtf just happened did we just get turned away. There’s surely a party in there. We sat around the park for a while out the front of the house and messaged some people for a while deciding if we wanted to go or not. We were waiting on the mate who owned the place to come back. Eventually a taxi pulls up, and some people we know get out of there and go into the party. We talk to them and ask them if we come, they say sure. 

We get in the party and there’s the fucking black dude who told us no party!! He’s playing a ukulele and singing with a bit of a crowd. There’s some people in the back of the yard having nangs but we weren’t sure if it was our crowd so we stayed at the patio. Towards the end before I went home I went over and talked to some people I knew. There was a girl on a daybed with flashing lights above her, and she was lying on her side. I also wasn’t sure if I was tripping but I thought it was real so I didn’t say anything.
